Subject: QuantaHealth RFP — Access governance questionnaire (SSO/SCIM/RBAC)

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for taking our call last week. Attached is the access governance worksheet from our RFP — the sections we're prioritizing are SSO (SAML/OIDC), SCIM for provisioning/de-provisioning, and RBAC/permissioning for clinical and analytics roles.

High level asks:
- Are you able to support both SP-initiated and IdP-initiated SAML flows?
- OIDC support for token refresh flows (authorization_code + PKCE) and session management.
- SCIM 2.0: bulk provisioning, PATCH for group membership, delta syncs, and typical rate limits.
- RBAC: mapping IdP groups to internal roles, role inheritance, admin role separation, and audit trails for permission changes.
- Retention windows for authentication logs and admin audit logs (we need 1 year minimum).

Please return completed worksheet by 2026-05-29. If you have an architecture doc and a short answers/pdf we can share with our security/compliance team, that would be helpful.

Attached: Quanta_RFP_Access_Gov_2026.xlsx

Regards,
Elena Park

Elena —

Thanks for the worksheet and the clear priorities. We've completed the questionnaire and attached a concise response packet (redwood-access-governance-responses.pdf) plus an architecture diagram that covers hosted and VPC/private deployment options (redwood-sso-scim-architecture.pdf). Key bullets below for your security team to skim: 

- SSO: We support SAML 2.0 (SP & IdP-initiated), full OIDC (authorization_code w/ PKCE, implicit not recommended, refresh token rotation supported), assertion/signature verification, optional assertion encryption, and configurable NameID/email mapping.
- SCIM: SCIM 2.0 support with PATCH, bulk creation, delta sync (since= timestamp) and incremental sync. Provisioning can be immediate or scheduled; de-provisioning supports soft-deactivate then purge.
- RBAC: Group-to-role mapping, role scoping by tenant or org unit, hierarchical roles, admin role separation (super-admin, org-admin, read-only auditor), and built-in approval workflows for permission elevation.
- Audit / Logs: Authn and admin audit logs retained 1 year by default in Hosted; Dedicated/Private customers can extend retention or export to customer S3/Cloud storage. All access logs include request_id, user_id, actor, change diff, and model route.
- Encryption & Keys: Data encrypted at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS1.2+). Customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) supported for Private installs.
- Identity features: Just-In-Time provisioning for OIDC, SCIM attribute mapping (email, displayName, department, custom attributes), SCIM group membership sync to enforce RBAC.

Open items we'd like to clarify with your security team: desired SCIM rate limits (calls/sec), retention SLA for audit exports (if you prefer longer than 1 year), and whether QuantaHealth requires assertion encryption or only signing.

I'm free to do a 30-minute technical deep-dive next week to walk through the architecture and SCIM behavior. Suggested slots: Tue 2026-05-26 09:00-11:00 PT or Wed 2026-05-27 13:00-16:00 PT.

Attachments: redwood-access-governance-responses.pdf, redwood-sso-scim-architecture.pdf, access_matrix.xlsx

Best,

Subject: Re: QuantaHealth RFP — Access governance questionnaire (follow-ups)

Vivek — thanks for the thorough packet, that helps a lot. A few clarifying items from our cloud identity team before we schedule the deep-dive: 

1) SCIM delta sync: can you confirm the canonical delta token behavior (opaque token vs since timestamp) and how you handle conflicts when an attribute is changed both in IdP and in Redwood within a short window?

2) Rate limits for SCIM: we need typical calls/sec for large orgs (10k-30k employees) and any recommended pacing for full bulk syncs.

3) De-provision timeline: when a user is deactivated via SCIM, what is the default enforcement for session termination and immediate access removal? Do you support emergency disable via API?

4) SAML/OIDC attribute mapping: if our canonical identifier changes (primary email), do you support stable immutable internal user IDs to avoid orphaned histories?

5) Audit retention: you mentioned 1 year by default. Please confirm encryption-at-rest details and whether logs exported to customer S3 are encrypted server-side as well. Also, can we get a copy of your SOC 2 Type II report or SOC cover letter?

If you can respond inline to the worksheet or provide a short appendix answering these five points before our internal review on 2026-06-03, that would help our timetable.

Thanks,
Elena Park
Procurement, QuantaHealth
